_comment: Hand-transcribed from pyk/src/tests/unit/test_kore_exec_covr.py at K v7.1.337
This is the ONLY test upstream has for any of K's coverage tooling, and because
the current haskell-backend no longer prints source locations in oneline format
(DebugAppliedRewriteRules.hs:69-73 now prints 'applied N rewrite rules'), it is
not a sample of a live format — it IS the specification. Nothing can regenerate it.
The upstream literals are Python raw strings (r'...'), so every backslash below is
a literal backslash in the input, JSON-escaped as \\. The escaped-space paths are
the point of those cases: do not normalise them.
See ../PROVENANCE.md for the transcription procedure and its verification.

parseHaskellOnelineLog._shape: id -> { line, entry, payload } ; entry is the HaskellLogEntry enum VALUE (kore_exec_covr.py:24-26)

cases.line: kore-exec: [5] Debug (DebugAppliedRewriteRules): /some/path\ with \ spaces/domains.md:1:2-3:4 /some/other/path\ with \ spaces/domains.md:5:6-7:8

parseRuleApplications._note: The multilocation line stays ONE composite space-joined key (kore_exec_covr.py:53-54 keys on the stripped payload verbatim); an empty payload becomes the literal key 'UNKNOWN'. Neither is a bug to fix.
